nodes.title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
nodes.trigger_detail: Masking: rolling window M=10 observations (SWE-agent; retune M=58 on OpenHands). LLM-Summary: fire when accumulated turns since last summary reach N+M (N=21, M=10). Hybrid defers summary and masks during accumulation.
nodes.notes: SWE-agent on SWE-bench Verified, 5 model configs, turn cap 250. Observation tokens ~84% of a SWE-agent turn (Lite-50). Masking halves cost vs Raw and matches/exceeds LLM-Summary; Qwen3-Coder 480B masking is 52% cheaper than Raw and +2.6% solve rate. Hybrid −7%/−11% cost vs mask/summary. LLM summaries can elongate trajectories by masking failure signals. Inference-only; no SFT on compacted spans.

nodes.title: Toward Reliable Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents: An Empirical Study of Execution Instability (TRACE)
nodes.trigger_detail: Recurrent compact when |z̄_{t+1}| > B (OpenClaw-style loop). Evaluated at B ∈ {16K, 8K, 4K, 2K}.
nodes.notes: AppWorld 147-task split; MiniMax-M3 frozen compressor+agent. At 16/8/4K FIFO matches or beats summary; only at 2K summary 72.8% vs FIFO 42.2%. Degradation is execution-state mislocalization (blocked/replay, wrong terminate), not fact loss. Repeated compact turns reliably-solved tasks into occasional ones (P@2 vs P^2 gap). Boundary-local PRE/POST verifier; 590 boundaries / 4640 rollouts; prompt optimized from preferences, models frozen. Code: github.com/nokia-applied-research/Trace.

nodes.title: Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks (AdaCoM)
nodes.trigger_detail: External manager edits the frozen agent's message list before every agent step (delete/merge/rewrite/no-op). No fixed token watermark.
nodes.notes: Qwen3-4B-Instruct manager: SFT warmup on GPT-5/Claude-Opus-4.6 edit traces, then RL (Trinity-RFT, G=8). BrowseComp-Plus mean@3 +39.0% avg vs ReAct across 4 agents (Kimi +95%). Fidelity–Reliability: strong ReAct agents keep more raw context; weak agents need aggressive compression. Transfer works across similar vanilla-ReAct capability. Untrained manager worse than ReAct (−8.9%). SumAgent/MemAct/SumCoM unstable across backbones. Agent frozen — no student SFT on compacted tokens.

nodes.title: LOCA-bench: Benchmarking Language Agents Under Controllable and Extreme Context Growth
nodes.trigger_detail: Context-editing (tool-result / thinking-block / compaction) fires at 200K for Gemini-3-Flash and GPT-5.2-Medium, 100K for DeepSeek-V3.2-Thinking. Tool-result clearing drops 50% of accumulated tool I/O; thinking-block clearing keeps only the latest think turn.
nodes.notes: Controllable env-state growth with fixed task semantics; models+scaffolds including context editing and tool-use CM. Same strategy can help one model and hurt another (memory/context-awareness hurt DeepSeek-V3.2 but help Gemini/GPT-5.2). Programmatic tool calling is the most consistent win (DeepSeek 10.7→24.0; GPT-5.2 38.7→49.3). Compaction on DeepSeek yields 13.3 acc but 1476-step trajectories. Claude Agent SDK at 128K env can drop vs native (26.7). Code: github.com/hkust-nlp/LOCA-bench.

nodes.title: Parallel Context Compaction for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Serving
nodes.trigger_detail: Compact when conversation length exceeds τ (swept 16k–96k). Parallel: partition into B-token blocks (sweep 16k→2k; 4k most stable).
nodes.notes: HotpotQA + LoCoMo; 4 backbones 8B–120B. Sequential summary output is nearly input- and prompt-invariant: 2k→96k input (+48×) yields only ~3× output (~3% retained at 96k); concise vs very detailed barely moves length. Sync compact is 14.5–62% of E2E wall time (15 fires at τ=16k vs 2 at 96k). Parallel block compaction gives operator volume control and better throughput at matched decode volume. Implication for SFT: do not try to steer the summarizer by prompt wording — identity of the compressor matters.

nodes.title: ContextBudget: Budget-Aware Context Management for Long-Horizon Search Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Before loading the next observation the policy sees b_t=(s_t, r_t, |o_t|) with r_t=B−|C_t| and must Null/Partial/Full-aggregate so |C'_t| ≤ B−|o_t|. Curriculum tightens B_max.
nodes.notes: BACM-RL = multi-turn GRPO; reward is F1 only if every turn respects the stage budget, else 0. >1.6× over strong baselines in high-complexity compositional QA / web browsing; advantage grows as budgets shrink. Over-compress under loose B and under-compress under tight B are the two budget-free failure modes. Compression decisions are in the same action space as reasoning (not a separate masked summary turn).

nodes.title: Slipstream: Trajectory-Grounded Compaction Validation for Long-Horizon Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Production-style aggressive compact well before the window; cites Anthropic 2026a: ~5–20k tokens for some workloads, ~50–100k for more complex tasks. Async compact overlaps next-k agent steps.
nodes.notes: SWE-bench Verified + BrowseComp; Qwen3.5-9B and Seed-OSS-36B. Sync compact is 26–44% of E2E latency. Slipstream +8.8 pp accuracy and −39.7% latency vs sync. 88–100% of first compaction-induced errors surface within 3 agent steps (boundary-local PRE/POST). ~90% of failures are omissions. Judge checks plan-level intent + statement-level facts. Code: github.com/chenzhuofu/slipstream. Inference-only validator, not an SFT recipe.

nodes.title: Less Context, Better Agents: Efficient Context Engineering for Long-Horizon Tool-Using LLM Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Always keep last N=5 tool call/response pairs; optional summary of the W=3 most recently evicted pairs (C4). Eviction is recency of whole tool units, not a token %.
nodes.notes: 50-task D365 F&O hotel itemization via MCP, GPT-5, 5 runs. Full history 71.0% complete / 1,480,996 tokens / 14.56 h. Last-5 prune 79.0% / 535,274 tokens / 5.39 h. Last-5 + W=3 summary 91.6% complete and 99.64% amount itemized / 553,374 tokens / 5.79 h. N=5 chosen because one line needs 2–3 tool calls. Inference-only; no student training.

nodes.title: AMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Memory for Agentic Applications
nodes.trigger_detail: Benchmark of memory Build/Retrieve, not a harness compact trigger. Mean trajectory ~57K tokens; synthetic subset scales horizon arbitrarily.
nodes.notes: 2496 real QA over Web/SE/Text2SQL/Embodied/Gaming/open-world plus synthetic. Existing memory (lossy summary + similarity retrieval) often loses to long-context baselines on agent trajectories. AMA-Agent causality graph + tool-augmented retrieval: 57.22% (+11.16% vs strongest baseline). GPT-5.2 long-context still only 72.26%. Warns that NL-style compression drops dense causal/objective tool state — relevant if SFT summaries are trained as NL condensates. https://ama-bench.github.io/

nodes.title: Governance Decay: How Context Compaction Silently Erases Safety Constraints in Long-Horizon LLM Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Harness compact when tokens(H) exceeds budget B; aggressive word-budget summarizer. ConstraintRot: policy turn → filler to B → self-contained prohibited tool request.
nodes.notes: ConstraintRot, 7 models, 1323 episodes. Violation 0% with policy in full context → 30% after one compact (59% DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi-K2.5). If constraint survives summary, violation 0%; if dropped, 38%. Soft org policies decay 8.3× more than hard safety norms. Compaction-Eviction Attack: optimized injection 0%→65% on a previously immune model. Constraint Pinning (~47 tokens, <0.5% of a production compact context) restores 0%. Decay is +0 if policy is in a preserved system message, +33–50 if in user/memory/tool channels.

nodes.title: DeepSeek-V3.2: Pushing the Frontier of Open Large Language Models
nodes.trigger_detail: test-time only: when token usage exceeds 80% of the 128K window, apply Summary (summarize overflowed trajectory and re-initiate), Discard-75%, or Discard-all
nodes.notes: No compaction-aware training. BrowseComp 51.4 → 67.6 with context management. Thinking-in-tool-use keeps reasoning traces across tool rounds and discards them only on a new user message.

nodes.title: Awesome Agent Context Compression (survey list + EMNLP 2026 survey)
nodes.trigger_detail: Taxonomy of who/when: system-controlled (token budget / step count), external controller, agent-controlled, learned. Survey Q=(D,R,P,O) eval axes.
nodes.notes: EMNLP 2026 Main survey 'Context Compression for LLM Agents' (Preprints 202605.2065). F1 pre-compress decision / F2 in-compress loss / F3 post-compress access. Eval section lists WebArena, AgentBench, MCP-Bench and calls for standardized CM benches (LOCA/TRACE/Slipstream/ConstraintRot are the dedicated ones). Coding-agent slice names Complexity Trap, AgentDiet, LoCoEval, TACO. Product/GitHub hop cap applied (4 outgoing).

nodes.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
nodes.trigger_detail: Observation-masking ACI: older tool outputs replaced by a placeholder (Complexity Trap's M-window is this mechanism).
nodes.notes: Defines the SWE-agent ACI used as the Complexity Trap masking baseline. 12.5% SWE-bench / 87.7% HumanEvalFix in the original paper. Observations dominate context; windowed elision is the default CM, not LLM summary.

nodes.title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Open-source LLM-Summary: condense older turns, keep a raw tail. Complexity Trap probes v0.43.0 with N=21, M=10.
nodes.notes: Production-style coding scaffold whose summary prompt is reused by Complexity Trap. Also a LOCA-bench integration target. Paper itself is a platform eval (SWE-bench, WebArena), not a CM ablation.

nodes.title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Every turn: rewrite a compact shared internal state from prior state + latest observation; discard the rest. Constant memory, not a token watermark.
nodes.notes: Cited by Complexity Trap, AdaCoM, ContextBudget, AMA-Bench. MEM1-7B is 3.5× better and 3.7× less memory than Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on 16-objective multi-hop QA. Complexity Trap notes MEM1 trajectories are hundreds of tokens, not SWE-scale. Internal state is the training target (preferred), not a masked summary span.

nodes.title: Reducing Cost of LLM Agents with Trajectory Reduction (AgentDiet)
nodes.trigger_detail: Inference-time delete of useless/redundant/expired trajectory spans (not a fixed % watermark). 'Delete' baseline drops whole turns instead of summarizing.
nodes.notes: Cited by Complexity Trap as concurrent LLM-Summary for SE agents. −39.9% to −59.7% input tokens and −21.1% to −35.9% cost at matched solve rate. Complexity Trap: their Delete baseline is more efficient than summary but severs reasoning traces and ignores that SE tokens are mostly observations.

nodes.title: Scaling LLM Multi-turn RL with End-to-end Summarization-based Context Management (SUPO)
nodes.trigger_detail: Periodic LLM summary of tool-use history to stay inside a working context; test-time can use more summary rounds than train-time.
nodes.notes: Lu et al.; Complexity Trap and TRACE cite it as summary-in-the-RL-loop for SE/CUA and search. Policy gradient treats tool-use and summarization as one policy. Success rises at same or lower working context; extra test-time summary rounds help hard search. Summaries are trained, not loss-masked.

nodes.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
nodes.trigger_detail: Issue-resolution bench; no native compaction protocol. Used as the substrate for Complexity Trap / Slipstream CM ablations (via Verified).
nodes.notes: Jimenez et al. ICLR 2024. Complexity Trap and Slipstream evaluate CM on SWE-bench Verified, not the original split. The bench itself does not trigger or grade compaction.

nodes.title: Introducing SWE-bench Verified
nodes.trigger_detail: Human-filtered 500-instance SWE-bench split used by Complexity Trap and Slipstream. No CM trigger.
nodes.notes: Chowdhury et al. 2024. The eval slice, not a compaction method. Complexity Trap runs full Verified; Slipstream uses it as the coding workload.

nodes.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
nodes.trigger_detail: Append-only thought/action/observation loop; no compact.
nodes.notes: Default no-CM baseline in Complexity Trap, AdaCoM, LOCA-bench, Context-Folding, AgentFold. AdaCoM uses vanilla ReAct score as the capability axis of the Fidelity–Reliability trade-off.

nodes.title: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
nodes.trigger_detail: External summary tool when context approaches the length limit; ReSum-GRPO then trains the agent to continue from those summaries.
nodes.notes: Cited by TRACE, AdaCoM, ContextBudget, Awesome. Training-free ReSum +4.5% vs ReAct; ReSum-GRPO +8.2% more via advantage broadcasting across summary-segmented trajectories. 1K samples suffice for a 30B agent. ACM (survey) later reports ReSum-style threshold summary underperforms plain ReAct on SWE-Verified (0.475 vs 0.489) — coding vs search discrepancy.

nodes.title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Compress observations and history via NL guidelines; no agent weight update. Distill the optimized compressor into a smaller model.
nodes.notes: Cited by TRACE, Less Context, Governance Decay, Awesome. Guideline search contrasts successful full-context vs failed compressed rollouts (same family as TRACE's frozen-proposer idea). AppWorld / OfficeBench / multi-objective QA: −26–54% peak tokens and better success; up to +46% for smaller LMs. Agent frozen; compressor distilled. ACM later: ACON-style 0.480 < ReAct 0.489 on SWE-Verified.

nodes.title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Stateful API world; earlier observations remain re-queryable. TRACE uses this to isolate execution-state failure from fact loss.
nodes.notes: 750 tasks, 9 apps / 457 APIs. GPT-4o ~49% normal / ~30% challenge. TRACE's FIFO≈summary result is specific to this refetchable setting. ACON also evaluates here.

nodes.title: OpenClaw agent-core recurrent compaction harness
nodes.trigger_detail: Recurrent compact when working context exceeds B; replacement context is the only history for later steps (TRACE adapts packages/agent-core/.../compaction.ts @ 0e7b5c3).
nodes.notes: TRACE's runtime. Also named by AdaCoM as a long-horizon app. Same loop used in AG2 / Hermes Agent per TRACE. Product hop; no further expansion.

nodes.title: Memory as Action: Autonomous Context Curation for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks (MemAct)
nodes.trigger_detail: Agent issues in-place memory edits (delete/insert/prune-and-summarize selected messages) as policy actions.
nodes.notes: AdaCoM baseline. MemAct-RL-14B matches models ~16× larger and cuts average context 51%. AdaCoM: asking the frozen agent to self-manage is unstable without agent-side training. Memory-edit tokens are on-policy actions (preferred in the manager/agent loss).

nodes.title: BrowseComp: A Simple Yet Challenging Benchmark for Browsing Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: 1266 hard web questions; no native CM. DeepSeek/Slipstream/AgentFold/AdaCoM (via BrowseComp-Plus) use it as a long-horizon pressure source.
nodes.notes: Wei et al. DeepSeek: 20%+ of cases overflow 128K, which is why the 80% CM exists. Slipstream's web workload. AgentFold-30B-A3B reports 36.2% here after SFT folding.

nodes.title: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Context-Folding (FoldGRPO)
nodes.trigger_detail: Agent branches a sub-trajectory and folds it on subtask completion, keeping a concise outcome summary (fold-on-branch-completion).
nodes.notes: Cited by AdaCoM and ContextBudget (Sun et al. 2025). Survey headline: 58.0% SWE-bench Verified at 32K active budget vs 55.2% for 327K ReAct; tool calls 72.8→96.5. Beats summary-based CM. Fold actions are trained with process rewards (preferred).

nodes.title: MCP-Bench: Benchmarking Tool-Using LLM Agents with Complex Real-World Tasks via MCP Servers
nodes.trigger_detail: 28 live MCP servers / 250 tools. No CM protocol. AdaCoM builds MCP-Bench-Wiki from its construction recipe; Less Context and Awesome list it as a tool-use bench.
nodes.notes: Breadth-oriented MCP eval. Less Context argues it does not isolate the token/accuracy trade-off of verbose tool dumps. AdaCoM's deep-research split uses a Wikipedia-MCP variant.

nodes.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents (Anthropic)
nodes.trigger_detail: Engineering post (2025-09-29): treat context as a finite attention budget; just-in-time retrieval; CLAUDE.md hybrid. Slipstream separately cites Anthropic 2026a for compact-at-5–20k / 50–100k — that later note is not on this 2025 page.
nodes.notes: Cited by LOCA-bench, Less Context, Parallel Compaction (Claude Code). Defines context rot and just-in-time file/tool retrieval. LOCA-bench implements Anthropic-style editing (tool-result/thinking/compaction) and memory/programmatic tools. Product hop; no further product expansion.

nodes.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
nodes.trigger_detail: Not a compact trigger; the U-shaped use-of-context result that motivates compacting before the window fills.
nodes.notes: Cited by Complexity Trap, Parallel Compaction, ContextBudget, Governance Decay. Parallel Compaction: the same failure hits the summarizer (96k in → ~3% kept).

nodes.title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents (LoCoMo)
nodes.trigger_detail: Multi-session dialogue memory bench (~9K tokens in AMA-Bench's table). Parallel Compaction uses it as a long-horizon accumulation workload, not a CM method.
nodes.notes: Cited by Parallel Compaction and AMA-Bench. Dialogue-centric; AMA-Bench argues it misses machine-generated causal tool trajectories.

nodes.title: AgentFold: Long-Horizon Web Agents with Proactive Context Management
nodes.trigger_detail: Each step the agent chooses a fold: granular condensation or deep consolidation of a finished sub-task. Not a token threshold.
nodes.notes: Cited by ContextBudget (Ye et al. 2025). AgentFold-30B-A3B: 36.2% BrowseComp / 47.3% BrowseComp-ZH with SFT only (no CPT/RL). Fold actions are SFT targets (preferred). Contrast with harness-controlled SFT-only continuation, which this project still treats as an open slice.

nodes.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
nodes.trigger_detail: Virtual context: agent pages working context to/from external memory when the window is pressured.
nodes.notes: Cited by AMA-Bench and Governance Decay as the OS-paging ancestor of compact/evict. Governance Decay: systems work (MemGPT, Slipstream, structured eviction) optimizes task accuracy, not constraint survival.

nodes.title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
nodes.trigger_detail: Terminus 2 'incorporates a context summarization module which makes calls to a language model to condense the agent's context when it reaches its model's context limit' — late, window-limit trigger.
nodes.notes: Cited by DeepSeek-V3.2 (TB 2.0, 89 tasks). Frontier <65%. DeepSeek 46.4 via Claude Code because thinking-CM is incompatible with Terminus (user-message-simulated tools); Terminus non-thinking 39.3. CompactionRL (survey) also uses full TB 2.0. The bench discusses compaction only as a Terminus implementation detail, not as a graded CM factor.

nodes.title: A Scalable Benchmark for Repository-Oriented Long-Horizon Conversational Context Management (LoCoEval)
nodes.trigger_detail: Repo-oriented conversational CM bench (iterative requirements, noise, retrospective Qs). Compares 4 CM methods + 3 backbones; authors add a unified conversational+repo memory.
nodes.notes: Listed under Awesome Evaluation / coding-agent slice. Standalone LLMs and generic memory systems struggle on repo conversations. Complementary to LOCA-bench (env-state growth) and AMA-Bench (agent-memory QA).

nodes.title: Context Compression for LLM Agents: A Survey of Methods, Failure Modes, and Evaluation
nodes.trigger_detail: Survey, not a trigger. Q=(D,R,P,O); F1/F2/F3 failure taxonomy used in the DSM-AE Stage-3 plan.
nodes.notes: YerbaPage et al.; EMNLP 2026 Main. Preprints.org HTML was blocked (Akamai); fields recovered from the Awesome README that is the survey's companion list. Calls out missing standardized CM benches — LOCA/TRACE/Slipstream/ConstraintRot fill that gap.

nodes.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
nodes.trigger_detail: Token-level prompt compression, not agent-turn CM.
nodes.notes: Cited by TRACE, Less Context, Awesome related surveys. Less Context: token deletion can corrupt verbatim ERP form state; they evict whole tool pairs instead.

nodes.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
nodes.trigger_detail: No CM. TRACE borrows Pass^k (solved in all k runs) vs Pass@k.
nodes.notes: Trivedi/Yao-style tool-user bench. TRACE uses k=2 Pass^k to show compression converts reliably-solved AppWorld tasks into intermittently-solved ones.

nodes.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models (GRPO)
nodes.trigger_detail: Not a compact trigger. GRPO is the optimizer under ContextBudget, ReSum-GRPO, FoldGRPO, AdaCoM-style group RL.
nodes.notes: Cited by ContextBudget. ReSum-GRPO broadcasts advantages across summary-segmented trajectories; ContextBudget zeros reward on budget violations. Relevant to how summary tokens enter the loss (usually the whole rollout, not mask-summary).

nodes.title: Context rot (Chroma)
nodes.trigger_detail: Documents accuracy drop with context length even when the fact is present — the reason products compact before the window.
nodes.notes: Linked from the Anthropic 2025-09-29 engineering post. Slipstream quotes 13.9–85% / 14–85% context-rot drops (Du et al. 2025 / this line of work) as why compact is now routine, not last-resort.

nodes.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Classic agent suite; Awesome Evaluation list. No CM protocol.
nodes.notes: Hop from Awesome eval section. Useful as a generic agent suite, not a compaction bench.

nodes.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: Web agent env listed in Awesome Evaluation. No CM protocol.
nodes.notes: Hop from Awesome eval section and OpenHands's original eval mix. Not a compaction study.

nodes.title: LOCA-bench code / env toolkit
nodes.trigger_detail: Implements the paper's context-editing and tool-use CM strategies (see arxiv:2602.07962).
nodes.notes: Open-source harness for the LOCA-bench paper. GEM-based; env/tools/tasks/scaffold decoupled.

nodes.title: TRACE code
nodes.trigger_detail: Implements TRACE's OpenClaw-adapted recurrent compact + PRE/POST verifier.
nodes.notes: Companion to arxiv:2608.06503. Product hop; no further expansion.

nodes.title: Slipstream code
nodes.trigger_detail: Implements async compact + next-k judge (see arxiv:2605.08580).
nodes.notes: Companion to Slipstream. Product hop; no further expansion.

nodes.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: fires when remaining budget < T_comp = 10,240 tokens (equal to per-response cap); resume = system + summary template + last k=2 atomic (a,o) steps; at most 3 compactions; peak B_active 64k (30B) / 80k (106B)
nodes.notes: PPO jointly trains execution and summary tokens under the task reward. w/o-summary-training (compaction on, summary turns masked) recovers most of the gain: 30B SWE-Verified compacted 50.5→54.5 vs 56.0 full; 106B 59.8→64.5 vs 66.8. Summarizer swap alone swings 49.0→55.5. No-compaction RL hurts compacted inference on 30B (50.5→48.0).

nodes.title: ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks
nodes.trigger_detail: agent calls manage_context (summarize + offload raw turns to disk) and query_memory; teacher injects when redundant queries / unproductive loops / sufficient context, and replaces premature calls; GPT-5.5 almost never invokes the tools
nodes.notes: On-policy distillation: teacher top-K=20 soft labels on all assistant tokens (manage_context included); system/user/tool-output masked. Resume-from-edit after teacher annotation. ReAct 0.489 → ACM-data 0.530 → +GPT-5.5 distill 0.564 on SWE-Verified. Threshold summary agents (ReSum-style 0.475, ACON-style 0.480) underperform ReAct.

nodes.title: Context as a Tool: Context Management for Long-Horizon SWE-Agents (CaT / SWE-Compressor)
nodes.trigger_detail: callable context tool at milestones: subtask completion, strategy switch, intermediate milestones, or context-growth/error-correction heuristics (not a fixed token threshold); workspace = Q + long-term memory M(t) + last-k raw ReAct steps
nodes.notes: CaT-Generator injects context-management Actions into complete ReAct trajectories then SFT+rejection sampling (drop failed trajs and unreasonable CM). CaT-Instruct ~20k trajs, avg 4.22 CM actions, 15.6k→4.7k tokens (30%). SWE-Compressor 32B 57.6% vs ReAct 49.8 and threshold-compression 53.8 on SWE-Verified.

nodes.title: Self-Compacting Language Model Agents (SelfCompact)
nodes.trigger_detail: rubric probe every N tokens (math) or N tool calls (search); fire if sub-task resolved or trajectory converging; suppress mid-derivation or when stuck; fallback fixed-interval baseline at 30% of max context (MiniMax-M2.5 / WebExplorer recipe)
nodes.notes: Training-free. Rubric is load-bearing: tool-alone is uneven; removing rubric drops accuracy 46.4%→41.0% (level with fixed-interval). +18.1 math / +5–9 search at 30–70% lower cost vs no compaction.

nodes.title: MemAgent: Reshaping Long-Context LLM with Multi-Conv RL-based Memory Agent
nodes.trigger_detail: document streamed in fixed chunks (paper: 5000-token chunks + 1024-token memory inside an 8K window); after each chunk the model overwrites the previous memory
nodes.notes: Multi-Conv DAPO: each chunk-update is an independent conversation; final-answer reward/advantage is broadcast to all preceding memory-overwrite generations. Memory tokens are the trained actions. Extrapolates 8K-trained model to 3.5M QA with <10% drop.

nodes.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
nodes.trigger_detail: Memory Manager runs ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP after each dialogue turn on extracted facts; not a token watermark
nodes.notes: PPO or GRPO on the manager's operation+content tokens; reward is downstream EM of a frozen Answer Agent. 152 QA pairs. Authors argue SFT is impractical because every memory op would need labels. External-bank memory, not working-context summarization.

nodes.title: COMPASS: Enhancing Agent Long-Horizon Reasoning with Evolving Context
nodes.trigger_detail: Context Manager synthesizes a progress brief each outer-loop turn; Meta-Thinker decides continue / replan / extract-answer; Main Agent runs a ReAct inner loop on the refreshed brief
nodes.notes: Hierarchical (Main / Meta-Thinker / Context Manager). Post-training pipeline delegates context management to a smaller Context-12B. Up to +20% relative on GAIA / BrowseComp / HLE vs single- and multi-agent baselines. Paper does not isolate whether brief tokens enter a student SFT loss.

nodes.title: SideQuest: Model-Driven KV Cache Management for Long-Horizon Agentic Reasoning
nodes.trigger_detail: auxiliary parallel task: the LRM reasons about token usefulness and evicts stale KV; management tokens are kept off the main reasoning context
nodes.notes: 215 hindsight-annotated traces teach deletion commands. −65% peak tokens on agentic tasks. Complementary to textual summarization: operates on the KV cache.

nodes.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models (ACE)
nodes.trigger_detail: Generator/Reflector/Curator loop incrementally updates a playbook; no intra-episode token watermark
nodes.notes: Cross-task evolving playbook, not intra-trajectory compaction. ACM Table 1 marks ACE Compact=✗. Warns against brevity bias and context collapse from iterative rewriting.

nodes.title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
nodes.trigger_detail: not an agent trigger: task-agnostic extractive prompt compression via a distilled token classifier
nodes.notes: ACON's extractive baseline. Student is trained with CE on keep/drop (or compressed text) labels distilled from GPT-4 — compressed representation is the training target. Not agent-history compaction.

nodes.title: WebExplorer: Explore and Evolve for Training Long-Horizon Web Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: SelfCompact/MiniMax-M2.5 cite the WebExplorer scaffold: when token usage exceeds 30% of max context, discard all history (Delete-all); 128K window, up to 100 tool turns
nodes.notes: SFT then RL on long-horizon web trajectories. The 30% discard-all recipe is the fixed-interval baseline SelfCompact beats. Paper itself is a web-agent trainer, not a compaction-loss study.

nodes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
nodes.trigger_detail: RL infrastructure (decoupled clip, dynamic sampling); no agent compaction trigger

nodes.trigger_detail: per dialogue turn extract facts then ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP into an external store (optionally graph memory)
nodes.notes: Heuristic operator set that Memory-R1 later RL-trains. Cross-session memory, not intra-episode working-context compaction. −90% token cost vs full-context.

nodes.title: Claude Code cookbook / auto-compaction (seed path)

nodes.notes: Seed id from seeds.json. The shipped auto-compaction notebook is at platform.claude.com/cookbook/tool-use-automatic-context-compaction (default context_token_threshold 100000). This seed path itself was not independently verified as a live page.

nodes.title: Automatic context compaction (Claude Cookbook)
nodes.trigger_detail: SDK compaction_control.context_token_threshold default 100,000 tokens
nodes.notes: Published 2025-11-24. Agent Python SDK monitors tokens per turn; when threshold exceeded, injects a summary prompt, model writes <summary></summary>, history is cleared, task resumes from summary only. Default threshold 100000. Recommends server-side compaction for Opus 4.6+.

nodes.title: Claude Code docs (seed)
nodes.trigger_detail: canonical pages now live under code.claude.com; see context-window and model-config
nodes.notes: Seed registry path. Current official compaction behaviour is documented at code.claude.com (context-window, model-config, how-claude-code-works).

nodes.title: Explore the context window (Claude Code)
nodes.trigger_detail: auto-compacts as you approach the model limit; /autocompact sets the window; /compact anytime
nodes.notes: After compact: system prompt unchanged; project-root CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules, auto memory, plan re-injected from disk; re-reads up to five most recently modified files (path-only if >5000 tokens); skill bodies re-injected with 5k/skill and 25k total caps. Subagent large reads stay out of parent context.

nodes.title: Model configuration — default auto-compact thresholds
nodes.trigger_detail: unset window: compact at model's context limit; Sonnet 5 default ~967K; 200K models compact at 200K boundary
nodes.notes: User can set auto-compact window via /autocompact 500k, --autocompact, autoCompactWindow setting, or CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW (env wins). Accepted 100K–1M, capped at model window. Sonnet 5 always 1M on Anthropic API and auto-compacts at about 967K unless CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 (then 200K).

nodes.title: How Claude Code works — when context fills up
nodes.trigger_detail: clears older tool outputs first, then summarizes if needed
nodes.notes: Official two-stage fill-up: older tool outputs cleared first; conversation summarized if still needed. Requests and key snippets preserved; early detailed instructions may be lost. Compact Instructions in CLAUDE.md or /compact with a focus. Stops auto-compact after a few thrashing attempts if one file/output immediately refills context.

nodes.title: Messages API server-side compaction
nodes.trigger_detail: compact_20260112 fires when input tokens reach a configured trigger; default not a published %
nodes.notes: Beta compact-2026-01-12. API summarizes, emits a compaction block, continues; later requests drop content before that block. Distinct from Claude Code client compaction.

nodes.title: Never Let Claude Code Auto-Compact Again
nodes.trigger_detail: practitioner: watch 30–50%, finish micro-task then compact ~50–60%; 1M windows treat 15–20% as reset band
nodes.notes: Anecdotal. Auto-compact is a seatbelt with no task-boundary awareness. Compact after a feature/tests, after root-cause, before research→implementation. Never mid-implementation. /compact KEEP/SUMMARIZE/DROP template. CLAUDE.md Compact Instructions. 1M: 15–20% practical reset (20% of 1M is already a large session).

nodes.title: How to Use the /compact Command in Claude Code
nodes.trigger_detail: practitioner 60% rule: run /compact at ~60%, not 80–95%
nodes.notes: Anecdotal 2026-04-02. At 60% the summary is written from uncompressed history; at 80–95% you summarize a degraded view. Append preservation instructions to /compact.

nodes.title: Claude Code /compact: What It Does, What Survives
nodes.trigger_detail: author states auto-compact at roughly 95% of the limit (not official)
nodes.notes: Anecdotal 2026-03-30. Manual /compact at task boundaries. compactPrompt in settings.json. PreCompact/PostCompact hooks for checkpoints. CLAUDE.md for durable rules. Author's 95% figure is not from current official docs (which use model-limit / ~967K for Sonnet 5).

nodes.title: Auto-compact cannot be disabled — measurements
nodes.trigger_detail: reporter: CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE Math.min-clamped to ~83%; one 1M session compacted at ~35%/346K
nodes.notes: Forum. v2.1.90 / Opus 4.6 1M. User claimed /config auto-compact false, autoCompactEnabled, DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT all ignored. Related issues cite ~78% and ~85% hard stops. Treat as user measurement, not official default.

nodes.title: OpenAI Codex CLI / IDE
nodes.trigger_detail: auto at model_auto_compact_token_limit (model-specific tokens, also clamped to ~90% of window); /compact manual
nodes.notes: Official slash-command docs: /compact summarizes the visible conversation. Config keys model_context_window and model_auto_compact_token_limit. OpenAI staff example for 1M Sol: compact at 900000. Source compact.rs keeps recent user messages up to COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS=20000 plus summary; local vs remote /v1/compact. PR #11516 clamps auto-compact to min(configured, 90% of context window).

nodes.title: openai/codex compact.rs
nodes.trigger_detail: token usage vs get_auto_compact_token_limit(); COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS = 20_000
nodes.notes: Local summarization prompt is a handoff for another LLM. Mid-turn compaction injects initial context above last user message because the model is trained to see the compaction summary last. Overflow while compacting trims oldest history to preserve prefix cache.

nodes.title: Codex Auto Compact on Terminal is completely broken
nodes.trigger_detail: users hit remote compact endpoint failures mid-session
nodes.notes: Forum 2026-04-29, Codex v0.125.0 / gpt-5.5. Error running remote compact task against chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses/compact. Confirms auto-compact is expected product behaviour even when broken.

nodes.title: Grok Build TUI user guide (compaction)
nodes.trigger_detail: auto at 85% of model context_window; [session] auto_compact_threshold_percent (default 85); /compact [keep note]
nodes.notes: Official local docs. /compact optional keep-instructions. context_window on [model.*] drives when 85% is reached (new custom models default 200000 if omitted). [features] two_pass_compaction default true; compaction_mode summary|transcript|segments. Memory: /flush before compact; [compaction.memory_flush] soft_threshold_tokens=4000 headroom; memory searched after auto-compact. Tool-result pruning: keep_last_n_turns=3, soft_trim 4000 chars (1500+1500), hard_clear_age_turns=10. Headless compact_boundary / auto_compact_* events. Plan mode state preserved. Public source mirror github.com/xai-org/grok-build (DEFAULT_AUTO_COMPACT_THRESHOLD_PERCENT=85).

nodes.title: xai-org/grok-build compaction crate
nodes.trigger_detail: DEFAULT_AUTO_COMPACT_THRESHOLD_PERCENT = 85; intra-compaction trigger_threshold_percent default 85
nodes.notes: Public mirror of Grok Build. Full-replace auto-compact at 85% of context_length.max_len. Intra-compaction also defaults to 85%, min_steps_before_compact=3, min_compactable_tokens=5000, max_reduction_ratio=0.8. Comment: shared ~85% trigger with Grok chat.

nodes.title: Training Composer for longer horizons
nodes.trigger_detail: research evals used fixed 80k and 40k token triggers; product default % unpublished
nodes.notes: 2026-03-17. Composer pauses at a fixed token-length trigger, is asked to self-summarize (~1k tokens vs ~5k prompted baseline), then continues with summary plus conversation state (plan, remaining tasks, prior summarization count). Same procedure is in RL training; final reward applies to agent tokens and self-summaries. Product forum: staff suggested /summarize around 70–80% when auto was late; no official shipping %.

nodes.title: Compaction not happening soon enough (Cursor forum)
nodes.trigger_detail: user: used to fire ~70–80%, now late at 90–100%; staff: try /summarize at 70–80%
nodes.notes: 2026-01-21. Confirms product auto-summarization exists and can fire late. Manual /summarize recommended. Distinct from Cursor 3.4 'compact chat' display density.

nodes.title: Cline Auto Compact
nodes.trigger_detail: when conversation approaches the model context-window limit; no published %
nodes.notes: LLM summarization replaces history and continues. Shown as a summarization tool call. Manual /smol alias /compact. Fallback to rule-based truncation on unsupported models. Checkpoints can restore pre-summary state.

nodes.title: Cline /smol (manual compact)
nodes.trigger_detail: /smol or /compact compresses in-place; user reviews summary
nodes.notes: Same action as Auto Compact but user-triggered. Unlike /newtask, stays in the same task. History after accept is the summary only.

nodes.title: Roo Code Intelligent Context Condensing
nodes.trigger_detail: slider default 100% of context-window usage; user can set e.g. 80%; plus 25% truncate on API overflow
nodes.notes: Enabled by default. Auto toggle + threshold slider + custom condensing prompt. Manual Condense Context button. Reserves ~30% of window (20% output + 10% safety) so ~70% is conversation. Overflow recovery truncates 25% and retries. Condensing always uses the active conversation model.

nodes.title: Continue conversationCompaction.ts
nodes.trigger_detail: compactConversation(sessionId, index) — user/index-driven; no published auto %
nodes.notes: Source helper summarizes history up to an index with a structured prompt (overview, active development, stack, …) and prepends 'Previous conversation summary'. Official docs did not publish an auto-threshold. Treat auto as unknown.

nodes.title: Aider token limits
nodes.trigger_detail: no conversation auto-compact; user /drop /clear /tokens; repo-map token budget --map-tokens default 1k
nodes.notes: Aider never enforces token limits; it reports provider errors. Context control is file-set management and a ranked repo map, not LLM history summarization. Infinite-output is output-limit continuation via prefill, not compaction.

nodes.title: OpenHands Condenser
nodes.trigger_detail: LLMSummarizingCondenser when event count > max_size (docs default 120; get_default_condenser often max_size=80); keep_first default 4
nodes.notes: Event-count, not token-%. Keeps first N + last M, LLM-summarizes the middle into a Condensation event. Also reactive on LLMContextWindowExceedError. Blog 2025-04-09: up to 2x cheaper, ~54% vs 53% solve. Fallback historically chopped history roughly in half.

nodes.title: OpenHands Context Condensation blog
nodes.trigger_detail: when conversation grows beyond a (unspecified numeric) threshold; summarize older, keep recent
nodes.notes: 2025-04-09. Bounded conversation size; summary encodes goals, progress, remaining work, critical files, failing tests. Extra turn used to condense.

nodes.title: SWE-agent history processors
nodes.trigger_detail: LastNObservations n=5 (classic paper config): older observations replaced by 'Old environment output: (n lines omitted)'
nodes.notes: No LLM /compact. Observation masking every step after the last n. Paper (arXiv 2405.15793): last-5-obs 18.0 vs full history 15.0 on SWE-bench. ClosedWindowHistoryProcessor collapses stale file windows. Breaks prompt cache unless polling workarounds.

nodes.title: mini-SWE-agent
nodes.trigger_detail: linear append-only history; no compaction documented
nodes.notes: Designed so trajectory == messages. No history processors. Context overflow is a hard limit unless the model window is large enough. FAQ contrasts with SWE-agent if you want history processors.

nodes.title: Managing context in GitHub Copilot CLI
nodes.trigger_detail: background compact ~80%; pause-wait ~95%; /compact anytime; tool output >20 KiB offloaded
nodes.notes: Official. Snapshot → structured summary (goals, done, files, next steps) → replace history with summary + original user instructions + current plans/todos; keep messages added during background compact. Tool output >20 KiB saved to temp file (COPILOT_LARGE_OUTPUT_THRESHOLD_BYTES). Checkpoints stored per compact. VS Code agent: chat.summarizeAgentConversationHistory.enabled; community source-trace ~0.78–0.82 warm / ≥0.90 cold.

nodes.title: How do I disable Summarized conversation history in Copilot Agent?
nodes.trigger_detail: VS Code setting github.copilot.chat.summarizeAgentConversationHistory.enabled
nodes.notes: Forum. Confirms IDE agent-mode history summarization is on by default and can be disabled. /compact added in VS Code Insiders Feb 2026 (discussion #177818).

nodes.title: Gemini CLI ChatCompressionService
nodes.trigger_detail: DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_TOKEN_THRESHOLD = 0.5 of model token limit; force=true for manual
nodes.notes: Source comment: if chat history exceeds this fraction of the model token limit, compress. PreCompress hook (Manual vs Auto). Community source read: preserve last ~30% aligned to a user-turn boundary; XML <state_snapshot>; second LLM probe/verify pass. Official product docs page for the 0.5 default was not separately fetched beyond this source file.

nodes.title: goose Smart Context Management
nodes.trigger_detail: auto-compact default 80% (GOOSE_AUTO_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=0.8); disable at 0.0; plus older tool-output summarization
nodes.notes: Official. Manual Compact now in UI. Customizable compaction.md template. GOOSE_TOOL_CALL_CUTOFF for how many recent tool calls stay full. Fallback strategies if still over: summarization / truncation / clear / prompt (CLI). Source: threshold<=0 or >=1 disables auto.

nodes.title: Amp: Handoff (No More Compaction)
nodes.trigger_detail: Oct 2025: /compact removed; replaced by /handoff (goal + relevant files into a new thread). Later reviews claim Neo 2026 re-added auto-compact — unpublished %
nodes.notes: Official 2025-10-23: compaction considered lossy and encouraged meandering threads. Handoff extracts a reviewed prompt + file list. Older CLI guides still listed /compact and amp threads compact. A 2026-06 review claims Neo (May 2026) auto-compacts near the window; no official numeric threshold found.

nodes.title: Windsurf Cascade
nodes.trigger_detail: official docs mention conversation summaries/checkpoints for @-mention of prior chats; numeric compact trigger unpublished
nodes.notes: Official Cascade page documents Memories, Todos, @-mention of previous conversations retrieving summaries and checkpoints rather than full transcripts. Unofficial trajectory reverse-engineering claims server-side CHECKPOINT steps when tokens exceed CheckpointConfig.token_threshold (value not published). Do not treat unofficial token_threshold as official.

nodes.title: OpenCode context compaction (community source-read)
nodes.trigger_detail: token_count >= input_limit − reserved; reserved = min(20000, model_max_output); /compact or /summarize; auto=false disables
nodes.notes: Widely used OSS coding agent. Community walkthrough of src/session/compaction.ts. Example: 200k input − 20k reserve → fire at 180k. Configurable compaction.reserved. Not an official opencode.ai docs page.

nodes.title: Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; OpenHands CodeAct append-only trajectories
nodes.notes: Filtered behavior cloning, not compaction-aware: 'rejection sampling fine-tuning (a.k.a. filtered behavior cloning), where we fine-tune the base LM on success trajectories sampled from SWE-Gym' — 491 successful teacher trajs (~19 turns, ~19k tokens). Failed trajs discarded. Per-instance cap later because training on all successes biases to easy tasks. PDF never mentions summary tokens or loss-masking compacted spans. OpenHands-LM-32B (37% SWE-Verified in follow-on cards) is this SFT lineage.

nodes.title: SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; SWE-agent teacher rollouts on synthetic bugs
nodes.notes: 'we fine-tune the base (or “student”) model on the trajectories corresponding to resolved instances' (RFT). 5,016 expert trajs from 20k Claude 3.7 runs; further cap ≤3 trajs per instance because 'easier' repeated successes degrade performance. Unresolved runs (~61% in later re-analyses of the public traj dump) are discarded, not rewritten. No compacted/summary-token loss rule.

nodes.title: Agent-FLAN: Designing Data and Methods of Effective Agent Tuning for Large Language Models
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; rewrites ReAct/JSON trajectories into multi-turn chat
nodes.notes: Rewrites, does not compact: 'we first replace the classical Thought-Action-ActionInput templates with multi-turn dialogues' and 'loss will be only applied to the assistant clause'. Capability-decomposed balancing + negative samples for hallucination. No summary-token rule. Closest industry-like default: assistant-only CE after format rewrite.

nodes.title: AgentOhana: Design Unified Data and Training Pipeline for Effective Agent Learning
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; unify heterogeneous trajs then AgentRater-filter
nodes.notes: Quality filter, not compaction filter: AgentRater scores whole trajs 0–5; keep score>=4 (167,918 sampled → 42,600 kept). Explicitly notes env reward can be high while intermediate actions are invalid. No mention of summary/compaction tokens in the loss.

nodes.title: FireAct: Toward Language Agent Fine-tuning
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; GPT-4 ReAct/CoT/Reflexion trajs unified to ReAct
nodes.notes: Fine-tune on 500 GPT-4 agent trajectories (and mixes of ReAct+CoT). Project page: 'These effective paths are then translated into the ReAct format' — keep successful/effective paths, rewrite format. No compacted-span loss rule.

nodes.title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; AgentInstruct = generate, interact, filter
nodes.notes: 1,866 trajs after 'trajectory filter'; GitHub: 'Ours are rigorously filtered using strict rewards to ensure top-notch quality.' Hybrid mix with general instructions. No compaction/summary loss statement.

nodes.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; two-stage SFT selection on resolved SWE trajs
nodes.notes: Closest SWE-SFT analogue of span masking, but for process-quality segments not summaries: 'During SFT, all segments remain in the sequence to preserve context, while only selected segments contribute to the loss computation.' Stage 1 keeps a 10% high-quality subset of successful trajs; stage 2 loss-masks low-contribution/risky segments. Cites SWE-Gym/SWE-smith as success-only SFT. Not a compaction paper.

nodes.title: From Patches to Trajectories: Privileged Process Supervision for Software-Engineering Agents (P2T)
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; privileged p* used to curate/shorten SWE-Gym trajs
nodes.notes: Compares outcome-filtered SFT to 'its tool-error-masking variant': error/tool-failure steps can be loss-masked while kept as context. Uses 1.8k curated SWE-Gym instances. Again not about summary tokens; shows SWE SFT already experiments with span masks, but on errors not compactions.

nodes.title: LLaMA-Factory / LlamaFactory
nodes.trigger_detail: No compaction/summarization trigger; SFT trainer only.
nodes.notes: Default DataArguments: train_on_prompt=False, mask_history=False (src/llamafactory/hparams/data_args.py). SupervisedDatasetProcessor._encode_data_example (src/llamafactory/data/processor/supervised.py) sets source_label=IGNORE_INDEX unless train_on_prompt, and target_label=target_ids unless mask_history and turn_idx!=0. Default therefore trains every assistant/function turn and masks user/observation/system. No filter drops 'summary' or compact messages. A compacted span is trained iff it is encoded as an even-position gpt/function turn; if it is human/observation/system it is context-only. mask_history=True would mask earlier assistant turns (including a mid-traj compact) and keep only the last turn.

nodes.title: Axolotl (now axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl)
nodes.trigger_detail: No compaction trigger; conversation masking only.
nodes.notes: Repo moved from OpenAccess-AI-Collective/axolotl to axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl. Default chat_template path: roles_to_train=['assistant'], train_on_eos='turn', train_on_inputs:false. Tool/user/system spans are masked; assistant (and optionally narrator) unmasked. Fine-grained message_field_training / train_detail / content-part train flags can mask a summary turn if the dataset author tags it. No built-in 'compact' or 'summary' drop filter.

nodes.title: Unsloth
nodes.trigger_detail: No compaction trigger; optional response-only mask.
nodes.notes: SFT via TRL SFTTrainer. Optional unsloth.chat_templates.train_on_responses_only (implemented in unsloth_zoo/dataset_utils.py:train_on_responses_only) string-matches instruction_part vs response_part and sets labels=-100 on instruction spans, including everything before the first response_part (system). Without that wrapper, conversational LM datasets train the full sequence. No compact/summary filter.

nodes.title: Hugging Face TRL SFTTrainer
nodes.trigger_detail: No compaction trigger.
nodes.notes: SFTConfig.assistant_only_loss defaults False (full-sequence loss on conversational language-modeling datasets). assistant_only_loss=True requires {% generation %}/{% endgeneration %} in the chat template and then ignores user/system. completion_only_loss defaults True only for prompt-completion datasets, None otherwise. Tool-calling SFT keeps tool role messages as context and trains assistant tool_calls. No compact/summary message type.

nodes.title: NVIDIA NeMo / Megatron-Bridge / Nemotron SFT
nodes.trigger_detail: No compaction trigger; role-based loss_mask only.
nodes.notes: Megatron-Bridge create_sft_dataset / GPTSFTDataset default answer_only_loss=True. Nemotron Super3/Nano3 Stage-1 SFT (docs/nemotron/super3/sft.md; src/nemotron/recipes/*/stage1_sft/data_prep.py) builds loss_mask=1 on assistant tokens and 0 on system/user, then packs. Tool-result roles are not a special 'summary' class; they follow the role table (non-assistant = 0).

nodes.title: OpenAI supervised fine-tuning docs
nodes.trigger_detail: SFT docs do not mention compacted sessions. Compaction is a separate Responses-API inference feature.
nodes.notes: JSONL chat format. Default: train on all assistant messages in an example. Optional assistant weight 0|1 disables loss on specific assistant turns (fine-tuning-best-practices). User/system/tool messages are context. Tool-call SFT trains assistant tool_calls and later assistant interpretations of tool output. No mention of compact/summary turns. Platform being wound down for new users as of the fetched page.

nodes.title: Amazon Bedrock / Anthropic Claude 3 Haiku fine-tune data format
nodes.trigger_detail: No compaction mention in FT data prep.
nodes.notes: Anthropic has no first-party public SFT API for Claude 4.x as of this scan. Only Claude 3 Haiku is listed for Bedrock fine-tuning. Data is alternating user/assistant messages plus optional system; assistant contents are the expected generated text. Docs do not say whether every assistant turn or only the last is in the loss, and do not mention compacted sessions.

nodes.title: LlamaFactory data/README.md (alpaca + sharegpt + tool roles)
nodes.trigger_detail: Format contract only.
nodes.notes: Alpaca: history prompt-response pairs 'will also be learned by the model'. ShareGPT: human and observation must occupy odd positions; gpt and function even positions; 'The gpt and function will be learned by the model.' System is a side column / first system_tag, not a trained turn. No 'summary' role. A /compact summary stored as human/observation is therefore context; stored as gpt/function it is a label.

nodes.title: LlamaFactory SupervisedDatasetProcessor._encode_data_example
nodes.trigger_detail: Token-level IGNORE_INDEX masking.
nodes.notes: Comment: 'for multiturn examples, we only mask the prompt part in each prompt-response pair.' encode_multiturn pairs messages 0-1, 2-3, ... so observation (odd) is source and function/assistant (even) is target. train_on_prompt copies source_ids into labels; else IGNORE_INDEX. mask_history reverses pairs (keep last turn under cutoff_len) and IGNORE_INDEX on all but the first reversed pair. PackedSupervisedDatasetProcessor drops examples with length>cutoff_len. Invalid examples (odd prompt length or response!=1) are dropped with 'Dropped invalid example'.

nodes.title: LlamaFactory arguments reference
nodes.trigger_detail: Documented defaults.
nodes.notes: train_on_prompt default False ('Whether to train on input prompts'). mask_history default False ('Whether to train only on the current dialogue turn'). packing default None (on in PT). neat_packing default False ('sequence packing without using cross-attention'). tool_format optional. DataArguments.__post_init__ raises if mask_history and train_on_prompt are both set.

nodes.title: LlamaFactory SharegptDatasetConverter / OpenAIDatasetConverter
nodes.trigger_detail: Role alignment; broken rows skipped.
nodes.notes: SharegptDatasetConverter maps user/assistant/observation/function/system tags (data_utils.Role). Odd tags = user+observation, even = assistant+function. Wrong tag at a position or odd message count → 'Skipping this abnormal example' and empty prompt/response (row discarded). OpenAIDatasetConverter folds tool_calls into function JSON and concatenates consecutive tool/observation messages. A compact summary with a non-standard role (e.g. 'summary') is not in tag_mapping and would break the row.

nodes.title: PR #9630 loss_mask for per-turn IGNORE_INDEX (not in fetched main)
nodes.trigger_detail: Proposed dataset field, not a runtime compact trigger.
nodes.notes: Opened Dec 2025 by CjangCjengh. Adds dataset loss_mask list aligned to messages; assistant turns with 0 are set to IGNORE_INDEX. Stated use: 'low-quality responses or context-only turns'. hiyouga LGTM 2025-12-18. Fetched main supervised.py (2026-09-01) does not contain loss_mask — treat as unmerged/not-in-main. Would be the first official way to mask a compact-summary assistant turn without mask_history.

nodes.title: Issue #8496 history thinking tokens still trained
nodes.trigger_detail: History CoT masking, not compaction.
nodes.notes: User reports that even when history thinking is stripped (DeepSeek-style), remaining history assistant text is still in the loss. Confirms default = train all historical assistant turns. Related DataArguments.preserve_thinking / mask_history + template.preserve_thinking. No compact/summary discussion.

nodes.title: Discussion #8838 mask_history for 'predict current step only'
nodes.trigger_detail: Maintainer points at --mask_history True.
nodes.notes: Multimodal multi-step dataset; author wants only the current-step answer trained. Maintainer hiyouga reply: '--mask_history True'. This is the documented last-turn-only path. Earlier compact/summary assistant turns would then be context, not labels.

nodes.title: Axolotl conversation / chat_template masking
nodes.trigger_detail: Role and per-part masks.
nodes.notes: roles_to_train:['assistant'] is the documented default for training all assistant messages. train_on_eos: turn|all|last. message_field_training / train_detail / content-part train|weight let a dataset mark a compact summary train:false while leaving later assistant turns trainable. Tool answers expected as role tool/ipython depending on template. No automatic drop of short/system/summary turns.

nodes.title: Axolotl config reference (roles, train_on_eos)
nodes.trigger_detail: YAML surface.
nodes.notes: Default roles map: user:[human,user], assistant:[gpt,assistant], system:[system], tool:[tool]. train_on_eos default 'turn'. Optional drop_system. No compact/summary key.

nodes.title: Hamel Husain: Axolotl train_on_inputs / template-free
nodes.trigger_detail: Masking tutorial.
nodes.notes: Documents train_on_inputs:false as 'one of the most popular features of axolotl': mask human/input, train outputs. type:input_output with per-segment label:true/false is the escape hatch to treat a compact summary as unlabeled context while training later tokens.

nodes.title: Axolotl PR #3625 multimodal assistant-only masking
nodes.trigger_detail: Fixes silent full-sequence SFT on VLMs.
nodes.notes: Apr 2026: VLM path had ignored train_on_inputs / roles_to_train / train_on_eos, training system+user+assistant. After the PR, role_boundaries scanner honors assistant-only and train_on_eos including 'last'. Confirms intended industry default is assistant-only, not full transcript.

nodes.title: unsloth_zoo.dataset_utils.train_on_responses_only
nodes.trigger_detail: Post-hoc label rewrite.
nodes.notes: Function train_on_responses_only(trainer, instruction_part=None, response_part=None, force_match=True) walks input_ids, finds response_part then next instruction_part, and unmasks only the assistant span. Masks system+user (everything before first response_part). get_chat_template_parts can auto-detect markers. A compact summary inside an assistant span is trained; one inside a user/system span is not.

nodes.title: Unsloth issue #1262 train_on_responses_only mismatch
nodes.trigger_detail: Marker mismatch can zero the loss.

nodes.title: Nemotron Super3 two-stage SFT loss mask
nodes.trigger_detail: Role table only.
nodes.notes: Pipeline: OpenAI chat format → chat template → role-labeled chunks → tokenize → loss_mask 1 for assistant / 0 for system/user → pack 4096. 'In SFT, we only want the model to learn to generate responses—not to predict prompts or system instructions.' A harness compact injected as user/system is therefore masked; as assistant it is preferred.

nodes.title: OpenAI fine-tuning best practices (weight)
nodes.trigger_detail: Per-assistant weight, not compaction.
nodes.notes: Multi-turn chat: include multiple user/assistant messages. 'Use the optional weight key (value set to either 0 or 1) to disable fine-tuning on specific assistant messages.' Examples set early assistant turns weight:0 and the last weight:1 — last-turn-only, user-controlled. Quality filter is human scrutiny / balance / no missing context, not dropping summaries. Examples longer than model example context (65,536 for gpt-4.1/4o) are truncated from the end.

nodes.title: OpenAI Responses API compaction (inference, not SFT)
nodes.trigger_detail: context_management compact_threshold; example 200_000 tokens.
nodes.notes: Server-side compaction for long Responses conversations. Emits an opaque encrypted compaction item, not a human summary. Docs never connect this item to the fine-tuning JSONL format. ZDR-friendly with store=false. Not a training-data recipe.

nodes.title: Azure OpenAI function-calling fine-tune format
nodes.trigger_detail: Tool-call SFT schema.
nodes.notes: Assistant tool_calls are training targets. Subsequent role=tool messages plus a following assistant utterance teach the model to interpret tool output. Tool payloads themselves are not described as labels. A compact summary in a tool or user message would be context.

nodes.title: Nebius SWE-rebench OpenHands trajectories + RFT
nodes.trigger_detail: Filter resolved=true; no compact step.
nodes.notes: 67,074 OpenHands v0.54.0 trajectories; 32,161 successful. RFT uses exclusively resolved=true. Average 64.3 turns, max 100, seq 131,072. Community r/LocalLLaMA 1puxedb. Dataset messages are system/assistant/user/tool — no summary role. Filter is success, not dropping compact spans.

nodes.title: Sequence Packing and Loss Masking in Production SFT (llms.blog)
nodes.trigger_detail: Survey of trainer masks.
nodes.notes: 2026-08-24 survey of TRL, Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory, Unsloth, NeMo. Three policies: (1) all assistant turns — Axolotl roles_to_train / NeMo / TRL if split; (2) last turn only — LLaMA-Factory mask_history=true, Axolotl train_on_eos:last; (3) weighted mixing — no native YAML. Open gap: 'Tool-call masking — environment-provided tool results should be masked like user turns, but only Axolotl's content-parts format handles this explicitly.' No framework names compacted agent summaries.

nodes.title: Raschka: When to mask prompt tokens during SFT
nodes.trigger_detail: Loss-mask semantics.
nodes.notes: Mask prompt tokens when the objective is p(response|prompt). IGNORE_INDEX/-100 excludes targets but keeps tokens as context. A compact summary in the prompt region is therefore kept_as_context, not discarded and not a label, unless the practitioner puts it in the response span.

nodes.title: OpenPipe ART additional_histories (compaction + subagents)
nodes.trigger_detail: Documents agents that 'compact their message history periodically'; no numeric trigger.
nodes.notes: Only industry trainer docs found that name compaction in the training schema. Trajectory.messages_and_choices is the live window; additional_histories hold pre-compaction (or sub-agent) conversations. Tokenization: main history first, then each extra history independently; 'training weight is distributed across all tokenized results'. Example puts 'Compacted conversation history: ...' as a user message in an extra History — that user text is context; assistant turns in both histories are trained. Pre-compact raw turns are kept as extra labeled trajectories, not discarded.

nodes.title: OpenThoughts-Agent-SFT-100K filter
nodes.trigger_detail: Quality filter: ≥5 model turns.
nodes.notes: 100k (task, trajectory) pairs from GLM-4.7-AWQ in terminus-2. 'filtered to traces with at least 5 model turns.' Filter is length/turn-count, not compact-summary content. conversations stored as role/content. No mention of dropping summaries.

nodes.title: Open-SWE-Traces distillation / pruning
nodes.trigger_detail: Behavioral pruning of loops/hallucinations, not compact spans.
nodes.notes: 207,489 OpenHands + SWE-agent trajectories. Stage-2 pruning removes suboptimal/hallucinatory patterns. Ablation: full corpus (including unresolved) beats resolved-only. No statement that compact/summary turns are preferred or dropped. Downstream SFT is standard next-token on the kept messages.

nodes.title: HF blog: packing with Flash Attention 2
nodes.trigger_detail: Packing attention isolation.
nodes.notes: Cited by the 2026 packing survey and by LlamaFactory neat_packing lineage. Packing concatenates examples; it does not rewrite or drop compact turns. Loss still depends on the upstream label mask.

nodes.title: MeetKai functionary contamination-free packing (neat_packing origin)
nodes.trigger_detail: Attention isolation for packed SFT.
nodes.notes: LlamaFactory changelog 24/07/04: neat_packing:true activates this packing. Prevents cross-example attention. Irrelevant to whether a compact summary is a label.

when: DeepSeek-V3.2 search-agent CM fires at 80% of the 128K window; Discard-all 51.4→67.6 BrowseComp, Summary 60.2 / 364 steps (less efficient). Thinking-CM keeps reasoning across tool turns and drops it only on a new user message — incompatible with Terminus-style user-message tools (arxiv:2512.02556).

Complexity Trap: SWE-agent masks observations older than M=10; LLM-Summary fires at N+M turns (N=21, M=10). OpenHands needs M retuned to 58. Hybrid masks during accumulation and treats summary as last resort. Any CM beats Raw; masking matches summary at half the Raw cost; Qwen3-Coder 480B masking is 52% cheaper than Raw and +2.6% solve (arxiv:2508.21433).

TRACE: compact when |z|>B. At 16/8/4K FIFO ≈ or > summary; only 2K favors summary (72.8% vs 42.2%). Failure is execution-state mislocalization; Pass^k decays under repeated compact. Prefer summary+raw-tail and boundary-local PRE/POST, not fact-retention scores (arxiv:2608.06503).

LOCA-bench: edit/compact at 200K (Gemini/GPT-5.2) or 100K (DeepSeek-V3.2); tool-result clearing drops 50% of tool I/O. Same strategy helps one model and hurts another. Programmatic tool calling is the most consistent win (arxiv:2602.07962).

Parallel Compaction: τ∈[16k,96k]; sync compact is 14.5–62% of wall time. Summary length is ~prompt-invariant (~3× output for 48× input). 4k blocks are the most stable operating point (arxiv:2605.23296).
ContextBudget: decide Null/Partial/Full aggregation from remaining budget r_t=B−|C_t| and pending |o_t| *before* loading the observation (arxiv:2604.01664).

Slipstream: production systems now compact well before the window (cites Anthropic 5–20k / 50–100k). 88–100% of first CM errors appear within 3 steps — use a 3-step PRE/POST window (arxiv:2605.08580).
Less Context: keep last 5 tool pairs; optional summary of the last 3 evicted pairs. 71.0%→79.0%→91.6% complete itemization vs full history, with ~63% fewer tokens (arxiv:2606.10209).
AdaCoM: there is no universal trigger — optimal fidelity vs compression tracks the frozen student's vanilla ReAct score (arxiv:2605.30785).
Governance Decay: one compact step takes violation 0%→30% (up to 59%) when in-context policies are not pinned; pin ~47 tokens of constraints outside the summarizer (arxiv:2606.22528).
Terminus 2 (Terminal-Bench) summarizes only at the model's context limit — the late trigger the rest of this literature treats as too late (arxiv:2601.11868).

Semantic alternatives to watermarks: fold-on-branch-completion (arxiv:2510.11967), AgentFold multi-scale fold each step (arxiv:2510.24699), MEM1 per-turn state rewrite (arxiv:2506.15841), ReSum/ACON near-limit summary (arxiv:2509.13313, arxiv:2510.00615).

Harness-controlled reserve: CompactionRL fires when remaining budget < 10,240 tokens, keeps last k=2 atomic (a,o) steps, caps 3 compactions; B_active is 64k/80k not the physical window. (arxiv:2607.05378)

Near-window / percent watermarks: ReSum at approaching the context limit (32k WebSailor); DeepSeek-V3.2 at 80% of 128K (Summary / Discard-75% / Discard-all); MiniMax-M2.5/WebExplorer Delete-all at 30%; ACM's Summary-Agent figure uses ~90%. (arxiv:2509.13313, arxiv:2512.02556, arxiv:2509.06501, arxiv:2607.23809)
Periodic length threshold L: SUPO resets to prompt⊕summary whenever |s_t|>L, with a max summarization-round cap S. (arxiv:2510.06727)
Dual compressor thresholds: ACON history iff |h|>T_hist and observation iff |o|>T_obs; agent never chooses the moment. (arxiv:2510.00615)
Semantic / rubric: SelfCompact fires after a resolved sub-task or converging trajectory and suppresses mid-derivation or when stuck; rubric ablation 46.4→41.0. (arxiv:2606.23525)

Agent tool at milestones: CaT injects at subtask completion / strategy switch / milestones; AgentFold folds every step (granular vs deep); Context-Folding folds on branch completion; ACM manage_context on redundant queries / loops / sufficient context — and teacher also teaches when NOT to compact. (arxiv:2512.22087, arxiv:2510.24699, arxiv:2510.11967, arxiv:2607.23809)
Mandatory every turn: MEM1 overwrites <IS> and prunes the previous turn; MemAgent overwrites a fixed memory after every document chunk. (arxiv:2506.15841, arxiv:2507.02259)
Strong teachers do not compact voluntarily: ACM observes GPT-5.5 almost never calls manage_context / query_memory, so compaction trajectories must be constructed. (arxiv:2607.23809)

sft: Almost all assigned eval/systems seeds are inference-time CM (Complexity Trap, TRACE, Slipstream, Parallel Compaction, LOCA-bench, Less Context, Governance Decay, AMA-Bench, DeepSeek 80% CM). They do not prefer, discard, or mask compacted spans in an SFT loss (arxiv:2508.21433, arxiv:2608.06503, arxiv:2605.08580, arxiv:2512.02556).

When training exists it is usually RL on the compressor/manager, not SFT-only continuation: AdaCoM SFT-warmup then RL on a frozen-agent manager (arxiv:2605.30785); ContextBudget GRPO with budget-zeroed reward (arxiv:2604.01664); ReSum-GRPO advantage broadcast across summary segments (arxiv:2509.13313); SUPO end-to-end summary+act (arxiv:2510.06727); MemAct RL prune actions (arxiv:2510.12635); FoldGRPO fold-on-completion (arxiv:2510.11967); MEM1 RL constant state (arxiv:2506.15841).

AgentFold is the clear SFT-preferred point: fold actions are SFT targets (no CPT/RL) and reach 36.2% BrowseComp (arxiv:2510.24699). ACON is the clear masked/frozen-agent point: guidelines + distilled compressor, agent weights untouched (arxiv:2510.00615).

Do not train a student on a prompt-similar summarizer: Parallel Compaction shows summary volume/content is nearly prompt-invariant and run-unstable at long inputs — compressor identity, not wording, is the control (arxiv:2605.23296).
AdaCoM: do not copy teacher compact policy onto a weaker student; Fidelity–Reliability says weaker agents need more aggressive compression (arxiv:2605.30785).

AMA-Bench: NL-style lossy summaries + similarity retrieval underperform long-context on causal/objective tool trajectories — if SFT uses summaries as targets, they must preserve tool-state causality, not chat condensates (arxiv:2602.22769).

TRACE/Slipstream imply SFT labels should be judged by next-3-step blocked/replay/intent, not ROUGE/fact retention; Pass^k (not just Pass@1) belongs on the compacted-eval card (arxiv:2608.06503, arxiv:2605.08580).
DeepSeek's 80% CM is test-time only; the paper does not state that compacted/discarded spans are SFT targets or loss-masked in the agentic synthesis pipeline (arxiv:2512.02556).

Load-bearing CompactionRL ablation: exposing the policy to compacted histories while MASKING summary-response turns (w/o-summary-training) recovers most of the compacted-inference gain (30B 50.5→54.5 of 56.0; 106B 59.8→64.5 of 66.8); putting summary tokens in the PPO loss adds the remaining +1.5/+2.3. (arxiv:2607.05378)

SFT papers put compaction/fold turns IN the loss as targets: CaT SFT on injected context-management Actions (rejection-sampled CaT-Instruct); AgentFold SFT on the folding directive block; SideQuest SFT on hindsight deletion commands (215 traces). (arxiv:2512.22087, arxiv:2510.24699, arxiv:2602.22603)

ACM on-policy distillation prefers assistant tokens including manage_context (top-K=20 teacher soft labels) and masks system/user/tool-output; student is then re-rolled from the teacher-edited turn (do not reuse the original suffix). (arxiv:2607.23809)

RL explorer vs SFT compressor split: ReSum SFT-distills ReSumTool on ⟨Conversation,Summary⟩ (summaries preferred for the compressor) but ReSum-GRPO trains only the explorer on post-summary segments with observations masked and the summary produced off-policy by the external tool; authors warn explorer SFT on ReSum trajs risks overwriting skills. (arxiv:2509.13313)

Joint RL treats summary/fold/memory-edit tokens as policy actions (preferred): SUPO, FoldGRPO, MemAct DCPO, MEM1 <IS>, MemAgent overwrite, Memory-R1 ops. CompactionRL argues GRPO-style group-norm mis-weights variable segment counts, hence PPO + token-level loss + cross-trajectory GAE. (arxiv:2510.06727, arxiv:2510.11967, arxiv:2510.12635, arxiv:2506.15841, arxiv:2507.02259, arxiv:2508.19828, arxiv:2607.05378)

Do not attention-mask deleted history in place: MemAct shows deleted tokens already sit in later KVs, so DCPO physically resegments; MEM1 instead rebuilds a 2D attention mask over a concatenated trajectory — SUPO says that still cannot train beyond the reliable window. (arxiv:2510.12635, arxiv:2506.15841, arxiv:2510.06727)

Compressor-only distillation (agent frozen): ACON CE-distills (raw hist/obs → compressed text) and keeps 95% of teacher accuracy; LLMLingua-2 is the extractive analogue. (arxiv:2510.00615, arxiv:2403.12968)

Mismatch is real: no-compaction RL can hurt compacted inference (CompactionRL 30B 50.5→48.0); CompactionRL gains do not transfer to single-window eval. Mix compacted and ordinary trajectories. (arxiv:2607.05378)

Cursor Composer is trained with compaction-in-the-loop RL: the same self-summary procedure used at inference is in the rollout; the final task reward is applied to all tokens including self-summaries, so good summaries are upweighted (preferred in the RL loss, not an SFT filter). Research triggers were 80k and 40k. [url:cursor.com/blog/self-summarization]

Academic compaction papers do not share one SFT loss. CompactionRL (RL) prefers summary tokens in the objective and only masks them in the w/o-summary-training ablation, which still gets most of the compacted-inference gain (arxiv:2607.05378).

When the summary is a policy action (AgentFold folding directive; Context-Folding return(message); SUPO LLM summary), those tokens are preferred / jointly optimized (arxiv:2510.24699, arxiv:2510.11967, arxiv:2510.06727).

When the summary is a tool Observation or new user prompt, academic recipes train the policy to continue from it and mask tool-outputs: ACM assistant-only distill with tool-output mask; ReSum-GRPO keeps s in q' and masks observations; ACON SFT is compressor-only CE and does not train the policy on summaries (arxiv:2607.23809, arxiv:2509.13313, arxiv:2510.00615).

CaT is the main SFT+offline-injection recipe: inject context-mgmt Actions, put teacher summaries in Observations, rejection-sample successes. The PDF never says whether summary Observation tokens are in the loss — mark unknown/mixed, not assistant-only by invention (arxiv:2512.22087).

SWE-Gym / SWE-smith / OpenHands-LM / FireAct / AgentTuning / AgentOhana filter or rewrite whole trajectories (success-only RFT, reward/AgentRater filters, ReAct↔chat rewrite). They discard failed or low-score trajs; they do not mention compacted spans. SWE-Prime and P2T later loss-mask low-quality or tool-error segments while keeping them as context — still not summary tokens (arxiv:2412.21139, arxiv:2504.21798, arxiv:2608.27449, arxiv:2605.21996).

Versus the expected industry default (LlamaFactory-style assistant-only next-token loss, no special compaction filter): academics either (i) up-weight/include summary tokens when the policy is the summarizer, (ii) mask them when a separate summarizer writes a tool/user span, or (iii) ignore compaction entirely and only success-filter raw ReAct traces. None publish an SFT corpus that discards compacted turns after they have been injected.

LlamaFactory default loss mask (DataArguments + SupervisedDatasetProcessor._encode_data_example): train_on_prompt=False, mask_history=False. Prompt/user/system/observation tokens get IGNORE_INDEX; every gpt/function (assistant) turn is a label. Alpaca history responses are also learned (data/README.md). Compacted spans are NOT discarded and NOT specially preferred. If the compact summary is stored as human/user/system/observation it is kept_as_context (masked). If it is stored as gpt/assistant/function — including a model-written /compact summary — it is trained as a normal assistant target. mask_history=True (optional; maintainer #8838) would mask those earlier assistant/compact turns and train only the last turn. Unknown roles or broken odd/even sharegpt rows are dropped (SharegptDatasetConverter). There is no short-turn or 'summary' filter. (github:hiyouga/LLaMA-Factory)

Industry trainers converge on assistant-only (or answer-only) loss, not on compact-aware filtering. Axolotl: roles_to_train=['assistant'], train_on_eos='turn', train_on_inputs=false; optional train_on_eos='last' or per-message train:false. TRL: assistant_only_loss defaults False on conversational LM data (full sequence) and True only if set; completion_only_loss defaults True for prompt-completion. Unsloth: opt-in train_on_responses_only masks instruction/system. NeMo/Nemotron: answer_only_loss=True / loss_mask 1 on assistant, 0 on system/user. None drop compact summaries. (github:OpenAccess-AI-Collective/axolotl, github:huggingface/trl, github:unslothai/unsloth, github:NVIDIA-NeMo/Nemotron)

OpenAI SFT trains all assistant messages by default; set weight:0 to disable specific assistant turns (including a summary turn if you choose). User/system/tool are context. Compaction exists only as Responses-API inference (opaque item; example compact_threshold 200000) and is not an SFT data type. Anthropic public FT is Bedrock Haiku alternating user/assistant only — no compacted-session language. (url:developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/supervised-fine-tuning, url:developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/compaction, url:docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/preparing-text-data.html)

Community SWE-agent/OpenHands/Claude-Code SFT recipes keep full tool trajectories and filter on task success (SWE-Gym 491 resolved; Nebius resolved=true RFT), min turn count (OpenThoughts-Agent ≥5), or loop/hallucination pruning (Open-SWE-Traces). They do not treat /compact summaries as preferred labels or drop them. OpenPipe ART is the exception that names compaction: additional_histories keep pre-compact raw conversations as extra trained trajectories and put the summary text in a user message (context). (arxiv:2412.21139, url:nebius.com/blog/posts/openhands-trajectories-with-qwen3-coder-480b, url:art.openpipe.ai/features/additional-histories)
